title: Test Cyberwave client context-manager cleanup without network access
body:
## Why
Cyberwave implements `__enter__` and `__exit__`, but the existing client tests do not directly cover context-manager cleanup. A focused regression suite will help preserve predictable cleanup for SDK users.

## Scope
Add tests for normal exit and an exception raised inside a `with client:` block. Keep SDK behavior unchanged.

## Start here
- `cyberwave/client.py`: `Cyberwave.__enter__`, `Cyberwave.__exit__`, `Cyberwave.disconnect`
- `tests/test_client_twin.py`: examples of constructing a client with mocked managers

## Acceptance criteria
- `__enter__` returns the same client.
- `disconnect` is called once on normal exit and on exceptional exit.
- An exception from the block propagates to the caller.
- Tests use mocks and do not contact MQTT, a backend, or hardware.

## Validation
`poetry run pytest tests/test_client_context_manager.py -v`

## Requirements
Python 3.10+ and the development dependencies; no API key or hardware.

## Getting started
Comment before starting so the maintainer can help scope the work.

title: Reject empty outbound Zenoh channel names in topic mapping
body:
## Why
`zenoh_to_mqtt` currently accepts `cw/12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789abc/data/` and returns an MQTT topic with an empty channel. Its documented contract returns `None` for keys that do not match the canonical channel pattern.

## Scope
Reject an empty channel segment without changing how valid channels, sensor suffixes, or MQTT prefixes are handled. Do not broaden this into a rewrite of topic validation.

## Start here
- `cyberwave/zenoh_mqtt/topic_mapping.py`: `zenoh_to_mqtt`
- `tests/test_bridge_topic_mapping.py`: `TestZenohToMqtt`

## Acceptance criteria
- Empty channels, including a key with an empty channel before a sensor segment, return `None`.
- Existing valid channel and sensor mappings remain unchanged.
- Add regression tests for both malformed shapes.

## Validation
`poetry run pytest tests/test_bridge_topic_mapping.py -v`

## Requirements
Development dependencies only; no broker, Zenoh service, API key, or robot.

## Getting started
Comment before starting so the maintainer can help scope the work.

title: Document prerequisites for four introductory SDK examples
body:
## Why
The examples index says that most scripts need an API key and some need extras, but newcomers cannot readily tell which of the first examples require a backend, simulation, or hardware.

## Scope
Document prerequisites for `quickstart.py`, `compact.py`, `joints.py`, and `locomotion.py` in `examples/README.md`. Read each script before making claims.

## Start here
- `examples/README.md`
- The four scripts under `examples/`
- `pyproject.toml` for supported extras

## Acceptance criteria
- Each entry states required extras, API/backend access, simulation support, and any hardware requirement.
- Distinguish 'no physical hardware' from 'works completely offline'.
- Preserve the existing links and descriptions.
- Avoid executing motion commands as part of this documentation task.

## Validation
Check every referenced script and extra exists; preview the Markdown and verify relative links. Explain in the PR which source code established each prerequisite.

## Requirements
Reading source files only; no account, API key, or robot.

## Getting started
Comment before starting so the maintainer can help scope the work.

title: Add worked examples explaining Zenoh-to-MQTT topic mapping
body:
## Why
Topic mapping has executable examples in unit tests and a short module docstring, but contributors need a small guide explaining prefixes, nested suffixes, and sensor segments.

## Scope
Add `cyberwave/zenoh_mqtt/README.md` with worked examples of the current mapping behavior. Link it from `CONTRIBUTING.md` as a hardware-free area to explore.

## Start here
- `cyberwave/zenoh_mqtt/topic_mapping.py`
- `tests/test_bridge_topic_mapping.py`

## Acceptance criteria
- Show both directions using a syntactically valid UUID.
- Explain MQTT prefix concatenation and the configurable inbound Zenoh prefix.
- Show that nested MQTT suffixes use underscores in the Zenoh channel, and that outbound sensor suffixes are dropped.
- Explain why mapping is not a lossless round trip.
- Include the focused test command and do not require starting either broker.

## Validation
`poetry run pytest tests/test_bridge_topic_mapping.py -v`; compare every worked example to the implementation/tests.

## Requirements
Development dependencies for optional verification; no API key, hardware, or running service.

## Getting started
Comment before starting so the maintainer can help scope the work.
